messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need to decide export routing strategy for multi-tenant spans/traces. Two options on the table: full per-customer siloing (separate indices/buckets per tenant) vs. namespace-tagged shared storage with RBAC at query time. Cost + retention implications for large customers are the sticking points. Thoughts?

jon: +1 to discussing. My hunch: split at the collector into tenant-specific exporters for the top ~10 heavy customers, shared namespace for the rest. That gives us clear retention policies for big payers without exploding exporters overall.

tara: Question: how do we implement the split in the collector without adding tons of config? We can use a processor to route by resource.attributes["redwood.tenant_id"] and then a simple exporter map. Example: 

```yaml
processors:
  tenant_splitter:
    action: split_by_attribute
    attribute: resource.attributes.redwood.tenant_id
exporters:
  elasticsearch/tenant-123: <config>
  elasticsearch/default: <config>
service:
  pipelines:
    traces/0:
      processors: [tenant_splitter]
      exporters: [elasticsearch/tenant-123, elasticsearch/default]
```

sam: We have to bake in deletion/retention per-tenant for GDPR. Physical separation (separate index/bucket) makes deletion trivial: drop index or delete bucket objects. Shared storage -> need to run tenant-scoped delete jobs that remove matching trace IDs and maybe reindex. That is operationally heavier and error-prone.

lee: Another angle is event fanout upstream: write to per-tenant Kafka topics (or a topic-partitioning key) and have dedicated consumers for the large tenants. That reduces collector complexity but shifts scaler complexity to consumers. Also helps if we want different retention backends (S3 vs ES).

pontus: Hybrid seems sensible. Proposal: 
- Tier 1 (top 10 customers): dedicated exporters -> dedicated indices/buckets, 1y retention (configurable per-contract).
- Tier 2 (all others): shared namespace with tenant attribute + query-time RBAC, 90d retention default.
- For GDPR deletion requests: Tier 1 -> index/bucket-level delete; Tier 2 -> soft-delete flag + async scrub job within SLA.

maria: This matches my thinking. Two operational questions: how do we enforce RBAC so engineering and CS can't accidentally query tenant X data? And how do we reflect this in the Console (rollout UX + dashboards)?

jon: For RBAC, enforce at the query layer (ES roles or BigQuery IAM) and map Console sessions to tenant-scoped tokens. On the Console side, hide the tenant selector when a user is assigned to a single-tenant role. For cross-tenant users (support) implement a temporary escalation workflow (timeboxed).

sam: Also log every admin query (audit trail) and surface in the Console audit timeline. That buys us compliance coverage.

otel-bot: otel-collector: rolling update queued to staging with tenant_splitter processor configured. Canary: 10 nodes.

tara: One more concern — metrics and dashboards. If Tier 2 is shared, dashboards must filter by tenant tag and be fast. We should precompute per-tenant aggregates into a metrics DB (rollup) to avoid heavy queries on traces. That will save cost and keep dashboards snappy.

maria: Action items: 
- jon + pontus to draft hybrid routing RFC with storage cost estimates and retention mechanics (due EOD Thurs).
- sam to draft GDPR deletion playbook for Tier 2 (how scrub job works + SLA).
- tara to prototype collector config for tenant_splitter and a minimal canary.
- lee to prototype a Kafka fanout PoC if we need decoupling between collector and exporters.

maria: Thanks all — marking as follow-up in the RFC channel. If no major objections I’ll formalize this into a design doc and link it in #eng-platform. :white_check_mark:
